result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, I'd recommend **Linear** if you're building a tech or SaaS company, and **Notion** or **Asana** if you're managing a broader mix of business, marketing, operations, and product work.

The best tool isn't necessarily the one with the most features. For a startup, it should be\:

- Easy to adopt without extensive training.
- Flexible as the team grows.
- Affordable at the early stage.
- Good for assigning ownership and tracking deadlines.
- Capable of keeping everyone aligned without creating unnecessary meetings or admin work.

## My top 6 startup project management tools

![Projects – Linear Docs](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/H7btCzSbelKXdMr_2WS3GWddG9qajBq9JZDHM8HYyOoLV6E4HDh5vlzogddffE6t5gTnGdoZ53UsXuMyPZWPmHRUwQ3ddApfS44CKAri923rLMIeylRQs9HZxmyB23G0rTfX3tmbKwJPdUtZW_x9bJsI8X8b5_Xrbg_k3vvdE22XkcL7igbp9gCGi9QLirCv?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Great for engineering and product teams.
- Fast, clean interface.
- Less suited to general business operations.

Pricing: Free tier; paid plans available.

[Explore Linear](https://linear.app/)

(Best all-in-one solution)

- Tasks, projects, docs, goals and dashboards.

Pricing: Free tier; paid plans available.

| Marketing / agency startup | Asana |
| 15–50 employees | ClickUp or Monday |
